Playbook.name: Kaspersky — Repeated Blocked Application Launches on One Endpoint - SOC Playbook

Reference.title: MITRE ATT and CK T1204 User Execution
MITRE ATT and CK T1219 Remote Access Software

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: Kaspersky Application Control blocked application launches repeatedly on one endpoint (GNRL_EV_APPLICATION_LAUNCH_DENIED, "Application startup prohibited"). The event message carries the object name, path, SHA256, KL category and the App-Control rule category (e.g. "ANY DESK"). Most bursts are benign policy enforcement (users repeatedly trying GameBar, Skype, games, or blocked remote-access tools); the concern is an actor persistently trying to run unsanctioned tooling - especially remote-access software - or a burst that coincides with a malware detection. The rule ships without an explicit ATT and CK mapping; the techniques above are best-fit for triage.
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: Repeated attempts to run controlled software may be a user working around policy (unlicensed / remote-access apps) or an attacker attempting to stage tooling. Only a small fraction are malicious, but a persistent attempt to run remote-access software on a bank endpoint warrants review.

Assets.AssetType: Windows endpoints managed by Kaspersky (App Control)

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Kaspersky Security Center CEF (verified live on logs-cef.log-*, cef.device.vendor == "KasperskyLab", observer.product "SecurityCenter"). Fields: destination.domain (the affected ENDPOINT, not the collector), destination.user.name (initiator, e.g. INTDOM\user), cef.device.event_class_id == "GNRL_EV_APPLICATION_LAUNCH_DENIED", cef.name ("Application startup prohibited"), message (multi-line: Object name, Path to object, SHA256, KL category, User, Result: Blocked, Rule category, Rule type). Pivot on destination.domain as the host of interest.

Signal.Name: Repeated Blocked Application Launches on One Endpoint
Signal.Details: A threshold of GNRL_EV_APPLICATION_LAUNCH_DENIED events for a single endpoint (destination.domain).

ImmediateCapture.Item: Read the message Object name / Path / Rule category to see WHICH application was blocked.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the full evidence story per the ClassificationGuidance. The blocked application's identity (remote-access tool vs game vs signed Microsoft app) drives the verdict more than the raw count.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the repeated launch denials are benign policy enforcement or a persistent attempt to run unsanctioned / remote-access / malicious software.

Step.name: Quantify the blocked launches on the endpoint
Step.Purpose: Count attempts and identify how many distinct users are driving them on this host in the window.
Step.Query: FROM logs-cef.log-* | WHERE cef.device.vendor == "KasperskyLab" AND cef.device.event_class_id == "GNRL_EV_APPLICATION_LAUNCH_DENIED" AND destination.domain == "$endpoint" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS attempts = COUNT(*), distinct_users = COUNT_DISTINCT(destination.user.name), users = VALUES(destination.user.name), signals = VALUES(cef.name) | LIMIT 1
Step.AnalystNotes: A high count from one user repeatedly launching the same app = benign nuisance. Spread across users or paired with malware alerts (see INV-03) raises concern.

Step.name: Read the blocked applications (object name, path, SHA256, rule category)
Step.Purpose: The message reveals exactly what was blocked - the decisive evidence for benign-vs-malicious.
Step.Query: FROM logs-cef.log-* | WHERE cef.device.vendor == "KasperskyLab" AND cef.device.event_class_id == "GNRL_EV_APPLICATION_LAUNCH_DENIED" AND destination.domain == "$endpoint" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | KEEP @timestamp, destination.user.name, cef.name, message | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 25
Step.AnalystNotes: Signed Microsoft apps (GameBar, Skype), games, or a known "ANY DESK"-category block = policy working. An unknown binary from a user-writable path (Temp / Downloads / AppData), an unfamiliar SHA256, or a remote-access tool (AnyDesk / TeamViewer / RustDesk) = investigate. Note the SHA256 for enrichment.

Step.name: Correlate with other Kaspersky activity on the endpoint
Step.Purpose: A launch-denial burst that coincides with malware / attack detections on the same host is a real incident, not nuisance.
Step.Query: FROM logs-cef.log-* | WHERE cef.device.vendor == "KasperskyLab" AND destination.domain == "$endpoint" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS events = COUNT(*) BY cef.device.event_class_id, cef.name | SORT events DESC | LIMIT 25
Step.AnalystNotes: GNRL_EV_VIRUS_FOUND*, GNRL_EV_ATTACK_DETECTED, GNRL_EV_ADSEC_DETECT or GNRL_EV_OBJECT_BLOCKED alongside the launch denials escalates to a host-compromise investigation. Device-control plug events alone are unrelated context.

Node.Condition: A persistent attempt to launch a remote-access tool (AnyDesk / TeamViewer / RustDesk) or an unknown binary from a user-writable path, and/or launch denials coinciding with a malware / attack detection on the host.
Node.Result: True Positive (Attempted execution of unsanctioned / malicious software - investigate host)

Node.Condition: The blocked applications are signed, known software (GameBar, Skype, games) that Kaspersky App Control is correctly denying per policy, with no threat context.
Node.Result: False Positive (Application Control enforcing policy as designed)

Node.Condition: App Control policy is over-blocking a legitimately needed business application, generating repeated denials for a valid user.
The blocked binary or its path / SHA256 is unfamiliar and cannot be classified from the logs alone.

FalsePositive.Definition: Application Control correctly blocking known / policy-controlled software.

Indicators.Item: Signed Microsoft or well-known vendor binary.
Known App-Control rule category (e.g. games, ANY DESK) firing as designed.
No malware / attack events on the host.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm the app and policy intent; close as policy_enforced (control working as designed).

TruePositive.Definition: An actor persistently trying to run unsanctioned / remote-access / malicious software, or a burst tied to a detection.

Indicators.Item: Unknown binary from Temp / Downloads / AppData with an unfamiliar SHA256.
Concurrent GNRL_EV_VIRUS_FOUND* / ATTACK_DETECTED on the host.

SOCAction.Item: Enrich the SHA256; isolate / review the endpoint; identify how the binary arrived; interview the user; open IR if malicious.

Misconfiguration.Definition: App-Control policy over-blocking a legitimately required application.

Indicators.Item: A valid business app repeatedly denied for a legitimate user.
Denials stop once an allowlist entry is added.

SOCAction.Item: Raise an App-Control allowlist request with the object name / path / SHA256; document.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Read the message to identify the blocked application(s), path and SHA256; determine benign policy block vs unsanctioned / unknown software.
Check for concurrent malware / attack detections on the same endpoint (INV-03); if present, treat as a host-compromise investigation.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: For unknown / malicious binaries: enrich the SHA256, isolate or review the endpoint, determine the delivery vector, remove the binary, and interview the user.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Tune the App-Control policy (tighten for remote-access tooling, allowlist legitimate business apps); reinforce software-request process; document lessons learned.

Escalation.Trigger: A blocked remote-access tool or unknown binary, or launch denials coinciding with a malware / attack detection on the endpoint.

FalsePositiveClosure.Item: Blocked applications confirmed as known / policy-controlled software with no threat context; closed as policy_enforced; allowlist request raised if a valid app was over-blocked.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Unsanctioned / malicious software identified and removed; delivery vector and user addressed; endpoint cleared; IR recorded.
